headline: Highest risk is medium: Khoj can read indexed notes while Whisper is local-only, creating modest prompt-injection and data-handling exposure but no direct write or network conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use RAG plus optional web search, so attacker-controlled content in its corpus could influence outputs. Whisper is a local speech model with no interactive tool use, so it is not itself an injection source, but if its transcripts are fed into Khoj the pathway exists. The pair lacks a direct shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are imported into Khoj's retrieval corpus without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF Khoj is configured to ingest untrusted notes or documents, malicious instructions can influence responses.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents.
Add a preprocessing step that strips instruction-like text from transcripts.
Review retrieved passages before acting on them.
Restrict Khoj collections to trusted sources only.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Whisper touches audio and speech. Whisper has no network egress and no file read access, so it is unlikely to exfiltrate data; Khoj's broad network egress could send retrieved content to configured search providers or cloud services. The pair does not share an OS workspace by profile, so leakage risk is limited and indirect.
conditions: IF Khoj is configured to send queries or retrieved snippets to external providers, notes may leave the local environment.
IF audio files processed by Whisper are later copied into Khoj, those contents can appear in Khoj outputs.
mitigations: Keep Khoj self-hosted with external search disabled.
Avoid placing sensitive audio transcripts into shared collections.
Audit outbound requests from Khoj for sensitive payloads.
Separate personal notes from transcription outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and Whisper likewise cannot write files or use network. With no overlapping write authority or mutable shared resource in the profiles, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway. The pair is therefore blocked by existing capability limits.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable state, the current none assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Reassess if an orchestrator adds locking-free shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate answers from retrieved notes, and Whisper produces transcripts from audio; if Whisper output is imported into Khoj, Khoj may treat it as authoritative without verification. Whisper itself does not act on downstream outputs, so the cascade is one-way and inferential, not directly observed. The main risk is incorrect transcription or retrieved text propagating into user-facing answers.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as source material for Khoj answers without human review, transcription errors can cascade.
IF Khoj is asked to summarize or act on retrieved notes, it may amplify upstream mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review of transcripts before indexing.
Mark transcription-derived content as untrusted metadata.
Add a verification step before Khoj answers are used externally.
Limit Khoj to summarization, not action-taking, for imported transcripts.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which may include regulated data, while Whisper touches audio and speech. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and Whisper has no network egress. Because the compliance surface is mostly on Khoj and the pair lacks a documented mismatch, this is a low, localized compliance concern rather than a breach by default.
conditions: IF regulated audio or notes are indexed into Khoj without policy review, compliance obligations may apply.
IF retention settings differ between transcription outputs and note storage, deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before indexing into Khoj.
Set explicit retention rules for transcripts and notes.
Keep regulated audio out of shared collections unless approved.
Document deletion/export procedures for both systems.
